subject: Migration incentives and bundle architecture discussion
messages:
From: Dana White <dana.white@brightlogix.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-15T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Migration incentives and packaging options

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for last week's demo. Procurement at BrightLogix asked me to follow up with a few concrete asks so we can compare apples-to-apples against our incumbent provider. High level: we need to understand what migration incentives you can provide, whether you can match per-token price for year 1, and what bundling/packaging options are available for our data residency + dedicated capacity needs.

Attached is our RFP excerpt and current commercial snapshot (BrightLogix_RFP_07062026.pdf). A few specifics we want to clarify:
- Is a one-time migration credit possible? If so, how large and any strings attached?
- Do you offer marketplace credits (Azure/AWS) instead of cash credits?
- Can you commit to a per-token price parity for months 1–12 while we ramp?
- How are VPC/private deployments priced vs hosted API?

Could you share a short proposal/pro-forma and a recommendation for the simplest contract construct that minimizes legal churn? We have a pricing review on Friday and would like something by Thursday EOD.

Thanks,
Dana White
Head of Procurement, BrightLogix
procurement@brightlogix.com

-----
Attachment: BrightLogix_RFP_07062026.pdf (application/pdf, 460 KB)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Dana White <dana.white@brightlogix.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-16T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Migration incentives and packaging options

Dana —

Appreciate the clear asks and the RFP excerpt. High level response up front: we can structure a competitive commercial that balances a one-time migration credit and marketplace credits, and we typically support an introductory per-token parity for a defined ramp window. I'll loop in Marissa (commercial lead) and Sergio (partnerships/marketplace) to draft a succinct proposal for Thursday.

Quick notes so we align internally:
- Migration credit: usually 10–25% of first-year committed spend (or equivalent token credit), depends on committed ARR and term.
- Marketplace credits: doable; we need to confirm Marketplace terms (timing of credit issuance, stacking with migration credit). Sergio — can you flag any constraints on Marketplace credit stacking?
- Per-token parity: we can offer a 12-month parity on our hosted API for a specific model bundle + usage threshold, but private/VPC pricing often carries a lift; we can do a blended concession.
- SLA/legal: simple addendum + SOW usually faster than full redline. We'll propose a clean SOW with an SLA annex.

Please attach any incumbent commercial summary (rates/commits) if you can — that helps us draw the parity construct.

I'll aim to have a proposal draft by EOD Thursday.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Dana White <dana.white@brightlogix.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-17T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal (high level) — options for BrightLogix

Dana —

Following Rishi's note, attached is a concise options matrix and a starter pricing sheet (redwood-proposal-BrightLogix-v2.pdf, pricing-sheet.csv). Summary of three options:

Option A — Migration Credit + 12m parity
- 12-month per-token parity to incumbent on hosted API for agreed model set (up to 24M tokens/month)
- One-time migration credit: $150k (applied as invoice credit over first 3 months)
- Standard hosted SLA; private deployment priced at +18% uplift

Option B — Marketplace-first (preferred by some customers)
- Equivalent economic to Option A but credit delivered as Azure Marketplace funds: $120k in marketplace credit + $80k migration support (professional services credit)
- Marketplace credit terms: issued after signup and verified consumption; cannot stack with certain publisher promos

Option C — Multi-year commit (best unit economics)
- 24-month commit with stepped discounts (year1 parity, year2 -15% off list)
- $200k onboarding credit and prioritized capacity placement

Open items we need from BrightLogix to finalize: incumbent per-token rates (CSV or screenshot), preferred credit mechanism (cash vs marketplace), expected monthly tokens for months 1–6.

If you can do a 30-min call tomorrow at 10:00 PT, we can walk the table and lock one option.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

-----
Attachments: redwood-proposal-BrightLogix-v2.pdf (application/pdf, 980 KB), pricing-sheet.csv (text/csv, 12 KB)
From: Dana White <dana.white@brightlogix.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-19T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal (high level) — options for BrightLogix

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few follow-ups after internal discussions:

1) Marketplace credits are preferable if they can be used to offset Azure billings immediately (we have a multi-cloud footprint but want Azure first). Your note about verification timing is a blocker if credits post after 30–60 days; we need credits applied within the first billing cycle if possible.

2) Our incumbent has a per-token blended rate of $0.00022 for our usage profile. To consider Redwood as a drop-in replacement, procurement needs a 12-month match for that blended rate on hosted API.

3) For private/VPC, we are willing to accept an uplift but need a clear number — propose +12% over hosted parity (not +18%).

4) We prefer marketplace credits over cash migration credit if you can make the arithmetic work (marketplace credits + pilot consumption allowance).

I'll attach a short incumbent price extract and our rough 1–6 month volume forecast. Can you confirm whether the migration credit can be split (50% marketplace, 50% invoice credit)?

Thanks,
Dana

-----
Quoted: On Fri, Jul 17, 2026 at 14:05, marissa_cole@redwood.com wrote:

>

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Dana White <dana.white@brightlogix.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-20T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal (high level) — options for BrightLogix

Dana —

Thanks for the clarity and for the incumbent extracts. I've reviewed with finance and legal and we can make an exception to support a blended commercial that meets your key asks. Final commercial summary we can commit to for an initial deal (subject to SOW/legal review):

- Per-token parity: Redwood will match the BrightLogix incumbent blended rate of $0.00022 on hosted API for 12 months for the agreed model bundle (up to 24M tokens/mo).
- Private/VPC: uplift capped at +12% over hosted parity (as requested).
- Credits: 50% of the migration incentive delivered as Azure Marketplace credits ($100k) issued within 45 days; 50% delivered as invoice credit ($100k) applied across first two invoices.
- Pilot: 60-day pilot allowance of 100k free tokens to validate integration and routing.
- SLA addendum: we will include a 99.9% availability SLA for hosted endpoints with a playbook for incident escalation; any additional contractual concessions to be captured in SOW.

Next steps: Marissa will create a formal proposal and we will open deal record DL-2026-0720-BL in HubSpot. Legal will prepare a short SOW + SLA annex for signature. If you agree, we can have docs to you by Tuesday EOD and an execution call next Thursday.

Marissa/Sales — please create the proposal and attach the pricing sheet and credit mechanics. Rishi — I authorize this as an exception under our competitive match policy; please escalate any last-minute asks.

Dana — if that construct works for BrightLogix, reply-all with confirmation and we'll advance.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
